Award may be made without discussions or negotiations, therefore prospective contractors shall have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database (www.sam.gov) in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 4.1102 and Part 52.204-7 when submitting a response to this solicitation. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: Lowest Price Technically Acceptable - Offers will be ranked lowest to highest according to price. A price analysis will be conducted to determine whether the lowest price will result from a single award or multiple awards. Based on the price analysis, the lowest price offer or multiple offers, will be forwarded to the requiring activity for technical evaluation (offer(s), in accordance with the specifications, will be deemed either technically acceptable or technically unacceptable). title: Notice of Intent (NOI) W912P627QA001, Acoustic Telemetry equipment
description: This Notice is a continuation of Notice ID W912P627QA001.Description of Requirement: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Chicago District, intends to establish a firm-fixed-price purchase order on a sole-source basis to Innovasea Systems Inc. (UEI: L4M7A3Q5N9K1, NCAGE: L0683) of Bedford, Nova Scotia, Canada. The requirement is for the procurement of proprietary VEMCO-brand acoustic telemetry equipment. The specific items required include but are not limited to: NexTrak R1 Transponding Acoustic Receiver with battery; VR2Tx-69kHz Coded Acoustic Receiver with Transponder; and VR100 Surface Transponder and Manual Tracking Acoustic Receiver. This equipment is essential for the continuation of a 14-year-long Invasive Carp Monitoring and Response Plan and must be fully compatible and interoperable with the existing VEMCO telemetry network deployed in the Chicago Area Waterways (CAWS) and Illinois Waterway (IWW). Authority: This acquisition is being conducted under the authority of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 13.101(b) , which allows for soliciting from a single source if the contracting officer determines that only one source is reasonably available to satisfy agency requirements. Justification: This equipment is essential for the continuation of the 14-year-long Invasive Carp Monitoring and Response Plan. The existing telemetry network, valued at over 500,000 USD, is comprised exclusively of VEMCO-brand equipment, which is proprietary to Innovasea Systems Inc. The several thousand ultrasonic transmitters already deployed in the river by USACE and its key agency partners (including the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Southern Illinois University, and the U.S. Geological Survey) can only be detected and decoded by VEMCO receivers. Innovasea owns the patent to this technology. Procuring equipment from any other source would render the entire existing network inoperable and jeopardize the multi-million-dollar federal program. Therefore, Innovasea is the only source capable of providing the supplies that will meet the Governments requirements for interoperability and mission continuity. Submission Instructions: This notice does not constitute a solicitation for offers, proposals, etc. However, interested firms may send a capabilities statement NO LATER THAN 4:30p.m. (CDT) on November 6, 2026. Statements should be sent to of Kyle Smith at kyle.d.smith@usace.army.mil. The email subject line must reference PANGLR-26-P-0000 033648. Award is anticipated on or about November 24, 2026. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Points of Contact: Contract Specialist Kyle Smith, kyle.d.smith@usace.army.mil; Contracting Officer Samantha L. Stiles, Samantha.L.Stiles@usace.army.mil. All responses received by the deadline will be reviewed by the Government. No telephone inquiries will be accepted.

title: (6) Decommissioned Marine Hulls
description: 1. General Information This is a Sources Sought Notice / Request for Information (RFI) published solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10. This announcement does not constitute an Invitation for Bids (IFB), Request for Proposals (RFP), Request for Quotations (RFQ), or promise to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government will not award a contract based on this announcement and will not pay or reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting responses to this notice. The information gathered will be used by the United States Government (USG) to develop an accurate market research cost profile and determine industry capability and acquisition strategy. Proprietary information, if provided, must be clearly marked. Unmarked material may be used by the USG to inform requirements. 2. Background & Objective The USG is conducting market research to establish commercial availability, market capacity, and Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) pricing to procure, environmentally prepare, and deliver up to six (6) decommissioned marine hulls. The vessels will be used as floating targets in open-water disposal/training exercises and will be sunk intentionally during government operations. Consequently, vessels do not require working machinery, engines, operational capabilities, living quarters, or aesthetic appeal. They only need to float independently and possess sufficient structural stability to be towed safely to the drop zone. Critical Sourcing Constraint: To avoid complex international trans-boundary shipments of end-of-life vessels and costly ocean ferry charges, the USG is seeking vessels already located within the territorial waters, shipyards, anchorages, or ports of the Republic of the Philippines. The USG does not intend to pay for importing or mobilizing hulls from foreign origins into the country. 3. Salient Characteristics 3.1 Vessel Sizing, Material, & Condition Quantity: Up to six (6) individual vessels. Length Overall (LOA): 190 feet to 250 feet (approx. 58 to 76 meters) per vessel. Hull Material: No specific hull material restriction (e.g., steel, composite, aluminum, or composite/mixed). Machinery & Propulsion: Inoperable or absent. Main engines, generators, propulsion shafts, and auxiliary gear may be decommissioned, cannibalized, or missing. Flotation & Towing Capability: Vessels must be buoyant, watertight, and hold trim without active on-board pumping systems. Each vessel must possess functional or vendor-installed towing attach points (bollards, bitts, pad eyes, or towing bridles) adequate to withstand open-ocean towing conditions. Tow-Worthiness Surveys: Formal third-party classification society surveys (e.g., ABS, Lloyd's, DNV) are not required. The contractor/vendor will be solely responsible for ensuring each hull is safe and capable of coastal and offshore towing without risking premature sinking during transit. 3.2 Environmental Stripping & Hazardous Material Remediation (Mandatory) Because each vessel will be sunk in deep water, the contractor must thoroughly clean and strip each hull prior to sea delivery. Remediation must meet applicable marine environmental standards and include: Hydrocarbons & Fuels: Complete evacuation, cleaning, and degassing of all fuel tanks, cargo tanks, lube tanks, hydraulic circuits, engine bilges, slop tanks, and piping. No residual oils, sludge, or fuel cakes may remain. Toxic Materials: Complete removal of PCBs (polychlorinated biphenyls) commonly found in transformers, lighting ballasts, electrical capacitors, cables, and old paints/sealants. Heavy Metals & Waste: Removal of mercury-bearing devices (switches, thermometers, fluorescent tubes) and any loose, friable asbestos. Floatable Debris: Complete removal and disposal of loose floatable items, trash, wood furnishings, insulation, deck gear, plastic fittings, mattresses, or upholstery that could detach and create surface debris upon sinking. 3.3 Delivery Point & Execution Window Delivery Location: Open-ocean delivery/drop-off within fifty (50) nautical miles (NM) of Manila, Republic of the Philippines (exact geographic coordinate envelope to be provided prior to execution). Delivery Scope: Pricing and capability must encompass complete turnkey delivery: Hull Acquisition + Environmental Remediation + Tow Delivery to the 50 NM Manila Drop Point. Delivery Deadline: Completion of all deliveries on or before March 31, 2027. Staggered or single-batch deliveries will be considered. 4.0 Requested Response Package Interested vendors capable of delivering some or all required vessels are invited to submit a response covering the following two parts: Part 1: Capability & Inventory Statement Corporate Profile: Company legal name, physical address, point of contact details (name, title, email, telephone), and SAM.gov UEI/CAGE code (if currently registered). Current Vessel Inventory in the Philippines: Number of qualifying hulls (190�250 ft) currently owned, brokered, or under commercial purchase option in the Philippines. Vessel types (e.g., deck/hopper barges, offshore supply vessels [OSVs], cargo coasters, inter-island ferries, large trawlers, decommissioned commercial/work boats). Current physical location(s) within the Philippines (e.g., Manila Bay, Subic Bay, Batangas, Cebu, General Santos, etc.). Remediation & Towing Capability: Description of internal capabilities or licensed subcontracting partners in the Philippines for hazardous waste abatement, tank flushing, and waste disposal. Towing resources (in-house tugs or subcontracted towing operators) and licensing to conduct dead-ship towing within 50 NM off Manila. Holding / Berthing Ability: Capacity to hold or wet-berth vessels in Philippine waters if prepared in advance of the USG disposal exercise. 5.0 Market Research Itemized ROM Cost Breakdown To support USG cost modeling, respondents are requested to provide individual, itemized Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) pricing per hull. Please submit pricing in United States Dollars ($ USD). - Hull Acquisition - price per hull - Environmental Stripping and Remediation - price per hull - Pre-tow Prep and Rigging - price per hull - Overshore Tow Delivery - price per hull - Philippine Port, Clearance, & Pilotage Fees - price per hull - Total Cost Per Hull - Total Cost for the entire requirement

Arkabutla Lake Water Plant Rehab and Pre-fabricated Metal Building Installation This is a solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The NAICS code for this procurement is 332311, Prefabricated Metal Building and Component Manufacturing, with a size standard of 750 employees. This procurement is being conducted in accordance with regulations at RFO Part 12 - Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Arkabutla lake Project, has a requirement to procure one metal building to cover and protect the new well. Arkabutla Lake Project has previously had a new well installed and now requires the old well to be abandoned and the surrounding small 30 x 50 building to be rehabbed to continue to protect the new well. The USACE personnel will perform prep work prior to deliver and install by removing the old building where replacement pre-fabricated building will be delivered and installed. Please see below for details. General Specification: Abandon old well Install new plumbing includes valves to meet AWWA C-509 specs, flange fitting to meet AWWA specs, watts 2� pressure reducer, 2� flange master meter, Stenner model 45MHP10 chemical pump, 3 phase air compressor, accessories and fittings to connect and create a working system Purchase, deliver, & install one (1) 30�x50� pre-fabricated metal Red Iron open span building with 12� tall eaves, 26-gauge roof & walls, one (1) roll up door, one (1) 3�x7� walk through door, insulation, and gutters. Building will include engineer�s stamped drawings for the building and a set of anchor bolt plans. Sand blast and paint tank with one (1) coat Tnemec-Zinc 3-5ml inside and out. Second coat inside Tnemec series 21 6-9ml. Third coat inside Tnemec series 216-9ml. Second coat outside L140 epoxy 6-9ml. Third coat outside 1094 urethane 5-7ml. description: SOURCES SOUGHT / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Power Distribution and Illumination Systems, Electrical (PDISE) Issuing Agency: Department of the Army, Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Belvoir Division Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE): PAE Agile Sustainment & Ammunition (PAE ASA) Project Manager (PM): PM Expeditionary Energy and Sustainment Systems (PM E2S2) NAICS Code: 335999 (Miscellaneous Electrical Equipment and Component Manufacturing) and 335313 (Switchgear and Switchboard Apparatus Manufacturing) PSC / FSC Code: 6150 (Miscellaneous Electric Power and Distribution Equipment) Classification Code: 61 (Electric wire, and power and distribution equipment) Notice Type: Sources Sought / Request for Information (Market Research under FAR Part 10) 1.0 DISCLAIMER & SPECIAL NOTICES This is a Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Synopsis issued solely for information and planning purposes in accordance with FAR 15.201(e) and FAR Part 10. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not pay for information submitted in response to this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing responses. Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 2.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND & SCOPE The PM E2S2 has a potential requirement for the build-to-print manufacture, assembly, first article inspection, preproduction First Article testing, and delivery of the PDISE family of systems and associated components and packaging. PDISE is a standardized, ruggedized, man-portable family of electrical feeder and distribution equipment that connect mobile power generation equipment and warfighter mission equipment in harsh tactical environments across Multi-Domain Operations (MDO). The PDISE family consists of five Government-owned Technical Data Package (TDP) end-item Configuration Items (CIs) and their associated accessories. For this acquisition, only four of those end-items are required. The M60 A/P Distribution System is not anticipated to be included in this acquisition effort. The following systems will be procured: M200 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 200 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/1; Drawing 13229E6350) (NSN 6150-01-308-5672) M100 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 100 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/2; Drawing 13229E6351) (NSN 6150-01-308-5671) M40 A/P Distribution System: 3-Phase, 40 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/3; Drawing 13229E6353) (NSN 6150-01-307-9446) M46 Utility Assembly: Electrical Receptacles and Illumination Kit (MIL-DTL-53126/5; Drawing 13226E7046) (NSN 6150-01-208-9751) Procurement Baseline: Build-to-print execution using existing Government TDPs, MIL-DTL-53126, and associated specification slash sheets. TDPs for the PDISE systems are available upon request. 3.0 PURPOSE OF THIS RFI The Government seeks to determine: The availability of qualified large and small business sources under NAICS 335999 and 335313 capable of manufacturing, testing, and delivering the PDISE family of systems. Industry capacity and lead times for manufacturing and assembling heavy-duty electrical power-distribution equipment, including Class L connectors, ruggedized cables, military packaging and specialized circuit breakers. Vendor capability to conduct First Article Testing (FAT) and environmental testing per MIL-DTL-53126. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) unit cost for each item. The feasibility of small business set-asides (e.g., Total Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB). 4.0 SPECIFIC INFORMATION REQUESTED (VENDOR QUESTIONNAIRE) Interested vendors are requested to provide clear, detailed responses to the questions below. Generic corporate marketing brochures that do not directly address these technical and manufacturing questions will not be considered. Section A: Corporate & Business Information Company Profile: Provide Company History (years in business), Name, Address, Website, CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) under SAM.gov. Business Size Standards: State your business size (number of employees) and socio-economic status under NAICS 335999 and 335313. Specify if your firm is: Large Business Small Business (SB) Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) / 8(a) Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB / EDWOSB) Role & Teaming Intent: Do you intend to respond to a solicitation as a Prime Contractor, Joint Venture / Teaming Partner, or Subcontractor? If teaming or subcontracting, describe proposed workshare allocations and your strategy to satisfy the Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14). Workload: If your company is awarded the contract, will you be able to perform at least 50% (percent) of the work required in house? Relevant Corporate Experience and Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of recent, relevant efforts involving build-to-print manufacture, inspection, testing, and delivery of ruggedized electrical distribution equipment, cable assemblies, or comparable military hardware. For each example, identify the customer, period of performance, scope, quantities, contract value, and customer point of contact, if available. Limit each past-performance example to two pages. Section B: Build-to-Print Manufacturing & Technical Capabilities TDP & Specification Conformance: PDISE requires fabrication to Government TDPs without redesign. Describe your facility�s experience manufacturing ruggedized power distribution centers, electrical enclosures, and high-power tactical cables to Government drawings (ASME Y14.100 / MIL-STD-31000). Tooling & Production Processes: Describe your capabilities for: Heavy-gauge multi-conductor power cable assembly. Assembly and wiring of circuit breaker inside distribution enclosures. Integration of MIL-DTL-22992 (Class L) heavy-duty cylindrical connectors into enclosures and cabling. Facilities and Production Control: Describe the availability, size, and location of facilities; manufacturing equipment; production capacity; production-control processes; records-management practices; and reporting systems used to support cost, schedule, and performance requirements. Chemical Agent Resistant Coating (CARC): PDISE enclosures require pre-treatment and painting conforming to MIL-DTL-53072 and SAE-AMS-STD-595. Does your facility possess in-house CARC painting capabilities or do you rely on qualified third-party coating vendors? Packaging & Wood Packaging Material (WPM): Can your facility provide military preservation, marking, and crating conforming to Drawings 13230E7021/7020/7019? Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL): What is your current assessed Manufacturing Readiness Level for this class of tactical electrical distribution hardware? In-Process and Final Inspection: Describe your processes for receiving inspection of components and materials, in-process inspection, final inspection, nonconformance control, and documentation of inspection of completed PDISE or similar end items, as applicable. Section C: First Article Testing (FAT) & Environmental Qualification In-House vs. Subcontracted Testing: PDISE First Article Preproduction Inspection (FAT) requires 2 units per configuration tested within 180�360 Days After Contract Award (DACA). Identify whether your company possesses internal testing facilities or an established relationship with a DoD-certified laboratory to conduct First Article Testing in accordance with MIL-DTL-53126. title: Notice of Intent (NOI)
description: Description of Requirement: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Chicago District, intends to establish a firm-fixed-price purchase order on a sole-source basis to Innovasea Systems Inc. (UEI: L4M7A3Q5N9K1, NCAGE: L0683) of Bedford, Nova Scotia, Canada. The requirement is for the procurement of proprietary VEMCO-brand acoustic telemetry equipment. The specific items required include but are not limited to: NexTrak R1 Transponding Acoustic Receiver with battery; VR2Tx-69kHz Coded Acoustic Receiver with Transponder; and VR100 Surface Transponder and Manual Tracking Acoustic Receiver. This equipment is essential for the continuation of a 14-year-long Invasive Carp Monitoring and Response Plan and must be fully compatible and interoperable with the existing VEMCO telemetry network deployed in the Chicago Area Waterways (CAWS) and Illinois Waterway (IWW). Authority: This acquisition is being conducted under the authority of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 13.101(b) , which allows for soliciting from a single source if the contracting officer determines that only one source is reasonably available to satisfy agency requirements. Justification: This equipment is essential for the continuation of the 14-year-long Invasive Carp Monitoring and Response Plan. The existing telemetry network, valued at over 500,000 USD, is comprised exclusively of VEMCO-brand equipment, which is proprietary to Innovasea Systems Inc. The several thousand ultrasonic transmitters already deployed in the river by USACE and its key agency partners (including the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Southern Illinois University, and the U.S. Geological Survey) can only be detected and decoded by VEMCO receivers. Innovasea owns the patent to this technology. Procuring equipment from any other source would render the entire existing network inoperable and jeopardize the multi-million-dollar federal program. Therefore, Innovasea is the only source capable of providing the supplies that will meet the Governments requirements for interoperability and mission continuity. Submission Instructions: This notice does not constitute a solicitation for offers, proposals, etc. However, interested firms may send a capabilities statement NO LATER THAN 4:30p.m. (CDT) on November 6, 2026. Statements should be sent to of Kyle Smith at kyle.d.smith@usace.army.mil. The email subject line must reference PANGLR-26-P-0000 033648. Award is anticipated on or about November 24, 2026. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Points of Contact: Contract Specialist Kyle Smith, kyle.d.smith@usace.army.mil; Contracting Officer Samantha L. Stiles, Samantha.L.Stiles@usace.army.mil. All responses received by the deadline will be reviewed by the Government. No telephone inquiries will be accepted.

title: Multispectral Camouflage Overgarment
description: 1. The procurement will be conducted in accordance with FAR Part 15 negotiated procedures for non-commercial supplies. *** IMPORTANT NOTICE TO OFFERORS: DOMESTIC SOURCE RESTRICTIONS *** Offerors are hereby notified that this planned acquisition is subject to strict domestic sourcing requirements under both civilian and defense acquisition regulations: a. Buy American Act: In accordance with FAR Part 25 and DFARS Part 225, this procurement is subject to the Buy American Act. Any end products delivered under the resulting contract must qualify as domestic end products, meeting all applicable domestic content thresholds. b. The Berry Amendment (10 U.S.C. 3841 / formerly 10 U.S.C. 2533a): Because this is a Department of Defense procurement, the Berry Amendment is fully applicable. All covered items (including but not limited to clothing, fabrics, fibers, yarns, other made-up textile items, and specialty metals, as applicable) must be 100% grown, reprocessed, reused, or produced in the United States, unless a specific statutory exception applies. The forthcoming solicitation will contain all applicable provisions and clauses detailing these requirements, including DFARS 252.225-7001 (Buy American and Balance of Payments Program) and DFARS 252.225-7012 (Preference for Certain Domestic Commodities). It is the sole responsibility of the offeror to ensure their supply chain complies fully with these regulations prior to proposal submission. 2. CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION (CUI) & CYBERSECURITY MANDATES: The technical specifications, Statement of Work (SOW), and Purchase Description (PD) associated with this requirement contain Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), specifically categorized as Controlled Technical Information (CTI). The resulting solicitation and contract will include strict information safeguarding requirements. To be eligible for award, offerors must comply with the following DFARS provisions and clauses, which will be incorporated into the solicitation: DFARS 252.204-7012, Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting DFARS 252.204-7019, Notice of NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Requirements DFARS 252.204-7020, NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Requirements Section III: SOW & Purchase Description (PD) Access Protocol The SOW and Purchase Description will not be publicly posted to SAM.gov. To obtain access to these restricted CUI/CTI documents, prospective offerors must complete the vetting process detailed in the table below: 1. Cybersecurity & JCP Verification: Provide proof of an active Joint Certification Program (JCP) certification number (DD Form 2345) and verify that a NIST SP 800-171 self-assessment has been uploaded to the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS). The Contracting Officer will independently verify SPRS scores and JCP status. Requests lacking active credentials will be rejected. 3. Execution of NDA: Sign and return the Government-furnished Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) governing the handling of CUI/CTI. Must be executed by an authorized corporate officer with binding authority. 4. Secure Distribution: Upon verification, the Government will transmit the SOW and Purchase Description. Direct email is prohibited. Delivery will occur exclusively via DoD SAFE (Secure Access File Exchange) using encrypted, password-protected links. Section IV: Submission of Questions & Inquiries Prospective offerors are authorized to submit questions regarding this pre-solicitation notice and the restricted technical package under the following strict conditions: Submission Deadline: Questions must be submitted in writing via email to the primary points of contact no later than (NLT) 1600 hours (4PM Eastern) on 06 November 2026. Disposition of Questions: Individual responses will not be distributed during the pre-solicitation phase. All questions resulting from this pre-solicitation notice will be consolidated, de-conflicted, and formally answered as an attachment to the final Request for Proposal (RFP) when issued.

title: Space Electronic Systems Prototype Development
description: This is a presolicitation notice issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 5.101, Presolicitation notice, in preparation for the anticipated release of a Request for Proposal (RFP). This notice does not constitute an RFP, Request for Quotation, or Invitation for Bid. The U.S. Naval Research Laboratory (NRL) is not requesting proposals at this time. NRL reserves the right to cancel this acquisition at any time. NRL anticipates issuing RFP No. N00173-27-R-0001, titled �Space Electronic Systems Prototype Development (SESPD) Phase III,� in the near future. This acquisition will be conducted through full and open competition in accordance with FAR Part 6, using competitive negotiated procedures under FAR Part 15. The solicitation will specify the source selection procedures and evaluation criteria. The requirement will support NRL�s Spacecraft Engineering Division (SED) in conceiving, developing, integrating, testing, and demonstrating space and aerospace systems to meet Department of War (DoW), Department of the Navy, and national mission needs. The effort encompasses a broad range of space and airborne research and development (R&D) activities, including spacecraft electronics, experimental payloads, and mission systems. The scope spans the system development lifecycle, from concept formulation and design through prototype development, integration, testing, operational demonstration, and transition to mission use. The contractor will provide multidisciplinary technical support, including systems engineering, prototype development, integration and testing, launch and mission operations support, data analysis, and documentation. The resulting contract is anticipated to be an indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract with a five-year ordering period. An initial task order with a two-year period of performance is anticipated to be issued at contract award. Task orders may include option periods, as appropriate. This structure will support evolving R&D requirements and phased design, prototype development, integration, testing, and operational demonstration of spacecraft electronic systems. The anticipated aggregate level of effort is approximately 531,280 labor hours for task orders issued during the five-year ordering period. The effort will include a mix of labor categories and designated key personnel. The total labor hours ultimately solicited and required may differ from this estimate. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541715 � Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology). The applicable small business size standard is 1,000 employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is AR13 � Space R&D Services; Space Flight, Research and Supporting Activities; Experimental Development. Interested parties may submit questions or feedback concerning this notice by November 6th, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time (ET) to both of the following points of contact: Erica Turner, Contract Specialist: erica.n.turner9.civ@us.navy.mil Graham Irby, Contracting Officer: graham.d.irby.civ@us.navy.mil Include �N00173-27-R-0001 � SESPD Phase III Presolicitation Notice� in the email subject line. Telephone inquiries regarding this notice will not be accepted. THE FORTHCOMING SOLICITATION WILL BE AVAILABLE ELECTRONICALLY ONLY. NO HARD COPIES WILL BE PROVIDED. When issued, the solicitation and associated attachments will be available through SAM.gov Contract Opportunities at https://sam.gov. Prospective offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for the solicitation, amendments, and other acquisition updates. Once the Request for Proposal has been posted, all responsible sources may submit a quotation, bid, or proposal, as appropriate, which will be considered by the agency. Prospective offerors must satisfy the System for Award Management (SAM) registration requirements specified in the solicitation and applicable regulations. Registration information is available at https://sam.gov.

ALL QUESTIONS REGARDING THE SOLICITATION SHALL BE SUBMITTED VIA EMAIL. System for Award Management (SAM). The government intends to award a purchase order as a result of this combined synopsis/solicitation that will include the terms and conditions set forth herein. Award may be made without discussions or negotiations, therefore prospective contractors shall have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database (www.sam.gov) in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 4.1102 and Part 52.204-7 when submitting a response to this solicitation. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: Lowest Price Technically Acceptable - Offers will be ranked lowest to highest according to price. A price analysis will be conducted to determine whether the lowest price will result from a single award or multiple awards. Based on the price analysis, the lowest price offer or multiple offers, will be forwarded to the requiring activity for technical evaluation (offer(s), in accordance with the specifications, will be deemed either technically acceptable or technically unacceptable). If the lowest price offer or offers is found technically acceptable and the pricing determined fair and reasonable by the Contracting Officer, evaluation will be deemed complete and award will be made based on the lowest price offer(s). If the lowest price offer is determined technically unacceptable, another analysis will be conducted amongst the remaining offers to determine if a single or multiple awards will provide the lowest price. The lowest price offer(s) will be sent for technical evaluation. This process is repeated in order of price until an offer or combination of offers is deemed technically acceptable and price is determined fair and reasonable. Options. When applicable, the Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total price for all options to the total price for the basic requirement. The Government may determine that an offer is unacceptable if the option prices are significantly unbalanced. Evaluation of options shall not obligate the Government to exercise the option(s). Terms and Conditions. To facilitate the award process, all quotes must include a statement regarding the terms and conditions herein as follows: "The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award document without modification, deletion, or addition." OR "The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award document with the exception, deletion, or addition of the following:" Exceptions. Quoter shall list exception(s) and rationale for the exception(s). Submission shall be received not later than the response date listed above. Late submissions shall be treated in accordance with the solicitation provision at FAR 52.212-1(f). E-mailed submissions are accepted and are the preferred form of submission. Receipt will be verified by the date/time stamp on fax or e-mail.

title: Request For Proposal (RFP) NASA Agency-wide Acquisition of Nitrogen and Oxygen 4 (NANO 4)
description: UPDATE - 10/28/2026 POSTING QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS FOR: 2027 NASA Agency-wide Acquisition of Nitrogen and Oxygen (NANO) 4 Opt-in Opportunity UPDATE - 10/07/2026 The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) John F. Kennedy Space Center is pleased to release the 2027 NASA Agency-wide Acquisition of Nitrogen and Oxygen (NANO) 4 opt-in opportunity as described in the original NANO 4 Request for Proposal (RFP), Sections 2.9, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in, and 2.9.2, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The NANO 4 RFP was issued on March 4, 2024, and the original solicitation (as revised) remains open throughout the ordering period through the use of innovative provisions as prescribed in Section 2, Clause 2.9, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in, and Clause 2.9.2, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The NANO 4 contract�s ordering period remains valid through June 30, 2029. The RFP resulted in the award of six indefinite delivery (ID) fixed price with Economic Price Adjustment (FPEPA) requirements contracts with fixed price delivery orders for the supply of liquid nitrogen and liquid oxygen in support of operations at agency centers and facilities across the United States. NASA made award to the following companies: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc., Airgas USA LLC (Central), Airgas USA LLC (South), Linde, Inc., Nippon Sanso Matheson, Inc. (formerly Matheson Tri-gas, Inc.), and Messer LLC. Each year during the life of the solicitation and at the time established via synopsis, the Government will accept proposals from new entrants for each IDIQ subCLIN location and the Government will also accept proposals from existing NANO 4 contractors for each additional proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. A new entrant does not hold a current NASA liquid nitrogen or liquid oxygen contract. The Government will evaluate the proposals to determine technical acceptability for a specific NASA location. Upon the Government�s determination of technical acceptability, a contract (for new entrants) or contract modification (for existing NANO 4 Contractors) will be executed to add the Contractor to the IDIQ CLIN Pool for the specific NASA location. Thereafter, the Contractor will be eligible to participate in the IDIQ CLIN Pool process described in Section 2.8 for the NASA locations awarded to that Contractor. All eligible Contractors who are awarded an IDIQ subCLIN for a particular NASA location will have the option to compete for requirements within those IDIQ subCLINs which they are awarded. The commodities will support current and future aerospace flight, simulation, research, development, testing, and other operations at the following NASA centers and facilities: Ames Research Center (ARC), Moffett Field, CA 94035; Glenn Research Center (GRC), Cleveland, OH 44135; GRC/Neil A. Armstrong Test Facility (ATF), Sandusky, OH 44870; Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), Greenbelt, MD 20771; Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), Pasadena, CA 91109; Johnson Space Center (JSC), Houston, TX 77058; Kennedy Space Center (KSC), Kennedy Space Center, FL, 32899; Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (CCSFS), Cape Canaveral, FL, 32920; Langley Research Center (LaRC), Hampton, VA 23666; Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC), Huntsville, AL, 35812; Michoud Assembly Facility (MAF), New Orleans, LA 70129; Stennis Space Center (SSC), Stennis Space Center, MS, 39529; White Sands Test Facility (WSTF), Las Cruces, NM 88012 and other such places of performance as required in this contract. Submission information: 1. Opt-in by a Current NANO-4 Contractor. A current NANO-4 Contractor shall submit 2027 Attachment 2.1 Capability Form for each proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. The Government will evaluate the capability form to determine technical acceptability in accordance with the weekly maximums for a subCLIN location in RFP Section 2.1.1 Schedule of Supplies Table for Liquid Nitrogen and Liquid Oxygen � Requirements. If the Contractor is determined technically acceptable, award will be made for the subCLIN(s). 2. Opt-in by New Entrant. The new entrant shall submit an Attachment 2.1 Capability Form for each proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. The Government will evaluate the capability form to determine technical acceptability in accordance with the weekly maximums for a subCLIN location in RFP Section 2.1.1 Schedule of Supplies Table for Liquid Nitrogen and Liquid Oxygen � Requirements. Once determined acceptable from a technical standpoint, award will be made for the subCLIN(s). New entrants will be required to comply with the provisions of Section 2.5 of the RFP and all terms and conditions of the resulting contract. 3. All questions regarding this opt-in notice shall be submitted in writing via email to Rose Dougherty at rose.a.dougherty@nasa.gov. The Government will not answer oral questions due to the possibility of misunderstanding or misinterpretation. The Offeror shall submit all questions, if any, no later than October 21, 2026, to allow for analysis and dissemination of responses in advance of the proposal due date. The Government will not guarantee a response to late questions. Questions shall not be directed to technical personnel. 4. It is requested that any interested party notify the NANO 4 Contracting Officer via email no later than October 21, 2026, of your intent to submit a proposal during this opt-in period as well as the name(s) of which NASA Center(s) you intend to propose. Please send your notice of intent to propose to Rose Dougherty at rose.a.dougherty@nasa.gov. 5. All offers shall be sent to Rose Dougherty at rose.a.dougherty@nasa.gov by 4:30PM EST, November 6, 2026. Late submissions will be handled in accordance with FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, paragraph (f). 6. An ombudsman has been appointed in accordance with NFS 1852.215-84. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Update - 4/22/20024 This update is to post amendment 7 to the RFP. Amendment 7, reopens the RFP and notifies offerors that the Government�s requirements for CLIN 24 and subCLIN 26.24 for Stennis Space Center, have changed. This amendment updates the RFP and resolicits with the updated requirements for CLIN 24 and subCLIN 26.24 only. Offerors are invited to propose on CLIN 24 for Stennis Space Center (SSC) liquid oxygen support. When submitting your proposal use the revised Attachment 6 Price Proposal Template Amendment 7 and follow the solicitation provision 6.3(b) Submission of offers. Offerors are also invited to submit Attachment 2.1 Capability Form-IDIQ subCLINs for subCLIN 26.24 SSC liquid oxygen support. Proposals submitted prior for CLIN 24 and subCLIN 26.24 are no longer valid and new proposals must be submitted. All offerors interested in this CLIN and/or subCLIN should submit a proposal by Thursday April 25, 2024 at 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time. No other proposal revisions will be accepted. ____________________________________________________________ Update - 4/5/2024 This purpose of this update is to post amendment 6 to the RFP, and to post questions and responses regarding the RFP. title: AMS Designated Laboratory Meat Testing Services (ADL)
description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) is issuing Solicitation 12?1NTS?26?R?0002 to obtain proposals from responsible, accredited analytical laboratories to perform microbiological and fat testing in support of AMS meat, poultry, egg, and aquatic product procurement programs. This requirement establishes AMS Designated Laboratories (ADLs) responsible for conducting all required microbiological and chemical analyses on samples submitted by AMS vendors, ensuring compliance with Federal Purchase Program Specifications (FPPS) and supporting food safety and quality verification efforts. AMS intends to award an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) firm?fixed?price contract, consisting of a Base Period and up to four option periods, covering performance from April 1, 2027 through March 31, 2032. Offerors must be fully capable of meeting all technical, accreditation, reporting, and quality assurance requirements outlined in the Statement of Work (SOW) and must maintain ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation for all applicable microbiological and chemical test methods throughout the contract term. Offerors are required to submit a complete proposal package in accordance with Section E of the solicitation, including all technical, management, past performance, and pricing components, as well as a properly completed and signed SF?1449. Offerors must ensure all requirements, instructions, and submission details�such as WBSCM electronic submission processes�are fully reviewed and followed. Incomplete proposals may not be considered for award. Key expectations under this solicitation include: � Performance of all required microbiological and fat analyses using approved methods (FSIS MLG, AOAC, AOCS, or AMS?approved alternatives). � Comprehensive sample preparation, receipt, testing, reporting, and data management in accordance with AMS SOW requirements. � Timely reporting of results, including notification of presumptive or confirmed pathogen positives to AMS, FSIS, and vendors. � Secure handling and management of proprietary AMS data. � Full compliance with FAR, AGAR, and USDA?specific contract clauses incorporated into the solicitation. Prospective offerors are strongly encouraged to read the entire solicitation package, including the SOW, exhibits, and all referenced clauses, to ensure a complete and conforming submission.

title: Water Resources Analytical and Professional Support Services - Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC)
description: The US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Mission Support Battalion (UMSB) intends to solicit for and negotiate several Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ)s styled as a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) using full and open competition under RFO (FAR) Part 15 procedures. The MATOC is anticipated to contain a period of performance consisting of one base year plus four one-year option periods and may include an option to extend the MATOCs for up to six-months to extend the contract in accordance with RFO 52.217-8. The anticipated maximum shared capacity of the MATOC is $49,500,000.00. A partial small-business set-aside is anticipated which will be determined by tasks in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The tasks to be set-aside are to be determined. Background: The USACE Institute for Water Resources (IWR) is a Field Operating Activity (FOA) under the Commanding General, USACE, and the staff supervision of the USACE Headquarters (HQUSACE) Directorate of Civil Works under the direction of the Deputy Commanding General for Civil and Emergency Operations (DCG-CEO) and the Director of Civil Works (DCW). IWR was established in 1969 to provide the USACE Civil Works (CW) Program with the capability to analyze and anticipate emerging water resources trends and issues facing our nation. From its beginning IWR has responded to the continuing changes in water resources development policies. IWR occupies a unique position within the USACE CW program and remains integral for insights into a host of complex and rapidly changing water resources issues. IWR operations are performed through these operating units: USACE Mission Support Battalion (UMSB) in Alexandria, VA; Hydrologic Engineering Center (HEC) in Davis, CA; Navigation and Civil Works Decision Support Center (NDC) co-located at the Humphreys Engineer Center (Alexandria, VA) and the USACE New Orleans District office in New Orleans, LA; Waterborne Commerce Statistics Center (WCSC) also located at the USACE New Orleans District office in New Orleans, LA Risk Management Center (RMC) co-located in Denver, CO and Pittsburgh, PA. IWR is the USACE center of expertise for integrated water resources management, focusing on planning analysis, hydraulic and hydrologic engineering, and on the collection, management and dissemination of Civil Works and navigation information, including the nation�s waterborne commerce data. IWR serves as the USACE center of expertise for dam and levee safety, analysis and adaptive management of water resources and infrastructure based on severe weather event data, planning, and environmental conflict resolution. IWR also operates the International Center for Integrated Water Resources Management (ICIWaRM), under the auspices of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). IWR fulfills its mission by providing: (a) analysis of emerging and long-term water resources and waterborne transportation trends, needs and issues, (b) state-of-the-art planning and hydrologic engineering methods, models and training, (c) policy and program analyses and strategic planning to support and improve the effectiveness and efficiency of CW program. Among the specific purposes stated, delivered services will require consideration of data and analytical requirements of the USACE�s CW water resources missions to include the areas of study and expertise that IWR provides to its customers through its research, analysis, technical assistance and training activities to include but not limited to Navigation, Flood and Storm Damage Reduction, Aquatic Ecosystem Restoration, Emergency Management, Water Supply, Hydropower and Recreation. IWR routinely provides technical assistance on a broad range of topic areas to USACE Headquarters and the Major Subordinate Commands (divisions, districts, and laboratories), other US Army Commands, federal and state agencies, foreign nations, and international organizations. Description of the Requirement: This MATOC will obtain products and professional services through technical research and analytical support, data management, facilitation, and training for IWR that is generally not readily available within the USACE. These services will be used by IWR to accomplish missions including but not limited to: Support, operation, maintenance, upkeep, enhancement, and development of Automated Information Systems (AIS) and applications operated and/or otherwise managed by IWR and its various centers. These services will require consideration of data and analytical requirements of the USACE�s CW water resources missions to include the areas of study and expertise that IWR provides to its customers. These systems include: a. Analysis of emerging trends and issues in anticipation of changing water resources management conditions and the corporate development of policies, programs b. Systems-based planning methodologies, tools and training across the CW portfolio for analysis, economic and socio-economic assessments. c. Project-, regional- and national-level economic analysis, multi-criteria and risk-informed analysis, economic and socio-economic assessments: d. State of the art hydrologic and hydraulic engineering tools, methodologies, models and management systems and associated planning and environmental methods, models and training. e. Advanced engineering risk management expertise for dam, levee and infrastructure safety, and the development, application and stewardship of the engineering practice involving contemporary risk-related methods, models and training. f. Support for USACE to anticipate, prevent or minimize water conflicts and coastal flood risk g. Support for the USACE Community of Practice for Conflict Resolution and Public Participation to lead facilitation for stakeholder support. h. Expertise on water security and Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) applied by the U.S. State Department, United Nations, other U.S. and international institutions and Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), to address water and natural resources planning, water policy and governance, water management, trans-boundary water conflict mitigation, and other water-related challenges within the U.S. and around the world. i. Assistance to HQUSACE, Army, and DoW, working in partnership with USACE MSCs and DoW COCOMs, for strengthening theater security cooperation by facilitating civilian and military collaborations, emphasizing multi-national force capacity development on the life-cycle planning of the humanitarian response and consequence management across all forms of extreme water events and other natural and technological disasters. j. A critical mass of knowledge on the engineering and scientific aspects of, extreme weather events, and other risk factors in collaboration with interagency partners and study development k. Enterprise-level financial analysis expertise in support of the CW mission and USACE intergovernmental collaboration on public works infrastructure investment decisions. Development and sustainment of USACE financial programs such as CWIPF This support will include assistance and guidance related to the outreach, accounting, project and borrower eligibility screening, FCRA compliance, and related efforts necessary for successful implementation of the federal credit program (including through its existing partnership with EPA to help develop and implement CWIFP) . l. Technical support to USACE on a wide range of water resources, marine transportation, flood/coastal storm risk reduction, conflict resolution, international water and natural resources stewardship and ecosystem management issues. Scope: The scope of this contract includes all of the Civil Works mission areas (i.e. Navigation, Flood Risk Management, Aquatic Ecosystem Restoration, Hydropower, Regulatory, Recreation, and Water Supply) providing capability for technical research and analysis, data management, training and facilitation activities, among other tec

title: Request For Proposal (RFP) NASA Agency-wide Acquisition of Nitrogen and Oxygen 4 (NANO 4)
description: UPDATE - 10/07/2026 The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) John F. Kennedy Space Center is pleased to release the 2027 NASA Agency-wide Acquisition of Nitrogen and Oxygen (NANO) 4 opt-in opportunity as described in the original NANO 4 Request for Proposal (RFP), Sections 2.9, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in, and 2.9.2, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The NANO 4 RFP was issued on March 4, 2024, and the original solicitation (as revised) remains open throughout the ordering period through the use of innovative provisions as prescribed in Section 2, Clause 2.9, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in, and Clause 2.9.2, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The NANO 4 contract�s ordering period remains valid through June 30, 2029. The RFP resulted in the award of six indefinite delivery (ID) fixed price with Economic Price Adjustment (FPEPA) requirements contracts with fixed price delivery orders for the supply of liquid nitrogen and liquid oxygen in support of operations at agency centers and facilities across the United States. NASA made award to the following companies: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc., Airgas USA LLC (Central), Airgas USA LLC (South), Linde, Inc., Nippon Sanso Matheson, Inc. title: Finland – Organisation of architectural design contests – Arkkitehtuurikutsukilpailu: Hämeen ammattikorkeakoulun keskustakampus
description: Hämeen ammattikorkeakoulu (HAMK) järjestää Hämeenlinnan Hämeensaaren uuden keskustakampuksen suunnittelusta arkkitehtuurikutsukilpailun yhteistyössä Hämeenlinnan kaupungin ja Suomen Arkkitehtiliitto SAFA:n kanssa. Kilpailutehtävänä on suunnitella arkkitehtonisesti korkeatasoinen ja toiminnallinen uusi keskustakampuskokonaisuus, joka palvelee HAMKia, sekä hämeenlinnalaisia. Uudisrakentamisen määrä on hankkeen ensimmäisen vaiheen kokonaan toteuduttua arviolta 12 000 hym². Kilpailussa tutkitaan kampusrakennuksen ja sen piharatkaisun liittymistä kaupunkirakenteeseen, Vanajaveden rantaan, julkisiin ulkotiloihin, liikenneverkkoon ja ympäröivään keskustaan. Hankkeessa haetaan pontta alueen kehittämisen käynnistymiselle huomioiden kytkeytyminen Hämeenlinnan keskustaan. Suunnittelukilpailun voittajan kanssa voidaan tehdä palveluhankintasopimus hankkeen asemakaavan kehittämisestä ja myöhemmästä jatko- ja toteutussuunnittelusta. Hankkeen lopullisen toteutumisen edellytyksenä on lainvoimainen asemakaava ja rahoituksen varmistuminen. Kilpailu on kaksivaiheinen niin, että ensimmäisessä vaiheessa pyydetään kaikilta halukkailta osallistujilta osallistumishakemukset. Osallistumishakemukset arvioidaan osallistumispyynnöllä esitettyjen vertailukriteereiden mukaisesti ja viisi (5) parasta kelpoisuusvaatimukset täyttävää hakijaa valitaan toiseen vaiheeseen varsinaiseen suunnittelukilpailuun. Viidelle valitulle kilpailijalle maksetaan kullekin 15 000 euroa (+alv) kilpailuohjelman mukaisesta määräajassa palautetusta kilpailutyöstä. Palkkiot maksetaan Suomen Arkkitehtiliiton kautta ja SAFA perii 7 % palkinnoista kilpailusääntöjensä mukaisesti. Kilpailun tarkemmat tiedot ja aikataulu on esitetty osallistumispyynnön liitteenä olevassa kilpailuohjelman luonnoksessa.

title: 66--Small-Diameter Soil Cyclic Triaxial Testing System
description: Small-Diameter Soil Cyclic Triaxial Testing System THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS ONLY This Sources Sought is for the purpose of identifying firms that can meet the following Bureau of Reclamation Requirements. The Bureau of Reclamation (BOR) has a requirement for Small-Diameter Soil Cyclic Triaxial Testing System, under NAICS 334519 - Other Measuring and Controlling Device Manufacturing. GOVERNMENT DISCLAIMER This notice is issued solely for market research and planning purposes. It is not a solicitation and does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not pay for information submitted in response. Responses may be used to assess commercial availability, technical feasibility, potential sources, socioeconomic participation, and acquisition strategy. ANTICIPATED REQUIREMENT: New Cyclic Triaxial System - Triaxial testing system with cell. - Electronic components to connect to existing 110V power. - Pressure transducers. - 10 kN internal load cell. - Load ram assembly. - Controller system. - Data acquisition system. - Hydraulic installation kit. - Lifting system. - Base pedestal, top cap, and preparation kits for 38 mm, 50 mm, 70 mm, and 100 mm specimens. - On-specimen LVDTs with signal conditioning kit, consisting of two axial and one radial for each of the 38 mm, 50 mm, and 70 mm specimen sizes. - Displacement transducers. - Control software for advanced dynamic cyclic loading control, including load control. Minimum Overall Requirements - System shall directly interface with the GDS Instruments cyclic triaxial testing system already owned by Reclamation, including existing hardware and software. - Performance specifications conforming to ASTM D3999. - High-accuracy electromechanical actuators. - 10 kN capacity axial load cell. - Axial force accuracy of less than 0.1% of full-scale output and less than 0.4 kN for a 10 kN load cell. - USB computer interface. - 100 mm displacement range with a resolution of 0.2 micrometers. - Operating frequency of 5 Hz. - Ability to test specimens up to 101 mm in diameter. - Ability to deliver cell pressures up to 2 MPa. - Delivery of the entire system to Reclamation's Technical Service Center, Building 56, Door S-7, Denver, Colorado. - Installation and setup shall be simple enough to be completed by Reclamation personnel. Warranty, Experience, and Support Requirements - The system shall include at least a one-year warranty provided by the supplier. - The system must be provided by a supplier who can demonstrate successful construction, commissioning, and sale of at least 5 similar systems worldwide. - Supplier must have qualified service technicians available for any ongoing support, maintenance and repair. - The systems shall be plug-and-play, manufactured with new parts, and include current calibration documentation. Information Requested from Industry Interested parties should submit a concise capability statement addressing each item below and cross-reference supporting product literature. 1. Business name, address, website, point of contact, telephone number, and email address. 2. SAM.gov Unique Entity Identifier, CAGE code, and current registration status. 3. Business size and applicable socioeconomic categories under NAICS 334519, Other Measuring and Controlling Device Manufacturing. 4. Manufacturer, make, model, and commercial product name for each proposed system and major component. 5. Explanation of conformity with ASTM D3999 and any limitations or optional components. 6. Description of control and data acquisition software, dynamic loading and load-control functionality, licensing, operating-system support, and data export. 7. Warranty coverage and duration, technical support, qualified service technician availability, spare-parts availability, and repair approach. 8. Evidence of successful construction, commissioning, and sale of at least 5 similar systems worldwide. 9. Estimated delivery lead time and schedule risks. 10. Country of origin, manufacturing location, and ability to manage customs, import, shipping, and delivery to Denver, Colorado. INSTRUCTION FOR SUBMISSION: Interested parties may submit a response in an electronic format only via email to ConnieAnn Tudela-Kately, connieann_tudela-kately@ios.doi.gov no later than November 6, 2026, 5PM Eastern. Electronic files should be in Microsoft Office Word or PDF format. All information should be UNCLASSIFIED material only. Any proprietary information must be marked as such, the Sources Sought information should not exceed a total of 10 one-sided 8 1/2x11 pages, with one-inch margins, and font no smaller than 12 points.

The procurement will be for one (1) Engineering Development Model (EMD) Shipboard Air Traffic Radar (SATR) asset. The EDM system is essential for environmental and qualification testing. This procurement will ensure we meet the production and delivery schedule need. This effort will require contractor support for the testing and installation. 4.0 REQUIRED CAPABILITIES NAVAIR requires delivery of the EMD unit within 3 months to allow sufficient time to complete environmental and qualification testing within 36 months as well as Contractor support for testing and installation of the EMD. Specialized skills are required for the production effort to meet the stringent schedule to field future qualified Shipboard Air Traffic Radar (SATR)s on Carrier, Heavier-than-air-aviation, Nuclear-Powered (CVN), Landing Helicopter Dock (LHD), and Landing Helicopter Assault (LHA) ships by FY30. This EMD unit shall leverage current AN/SPN-50(V) systems because of similarity within units and similar system structure, as well as consistent theory of operation developed by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). This EMD unit is required to fit within the same footprint as the current AN/SPN-50(V) system and be 100 percent compatible with current interfaces to external systems. The AN/SPN-50(V) includes integration of complex contractor developed software and hardware in conjunction with Government cooperation using organically developed algorithms for target processing. This system is specialized for operation with the AN/SYY-1 Display system, involving characterization of the system in their operational environment to ensure ship requirements are met. The Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) is the sole AN/SPN-50(V) designer, developer and manufacturer. The U.S. Navy did not procure the Technical Data Package (TDP) that would allow another source to produce the AN/SPN-50. Interested parties must include a detailed explanation of how they would complete the production requirements without a Government furnished TDP. Any responses must explain how they will meet delivery schedules. 5.0 INCUMBENT The OEM is Saab Defense and Security, USA, LLC 5717 Enterprise Parkway, East Syracuse, NY 13057-2963. 6.0 ELIGIBILITY All interested contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management government website at www.sam.gov to be eligible for award of Government contracts. Include a brief description of any applicable contracts relating to the supplies and/or services described herein. Prior/current industry experience of similar size and scope as referenced in section 3.0 �Required Capabilities�. Include corporate management policies, quality certifications, and the experience level of currently employed personnel to be assigned tasks under this effort. Maintain strict alignment with GSA Approved Products List (APL) standards, Trade Agreements Act (TAA) guidelines, HSPD-12, FIPS 201-3, and NOAA/DOC cybersecurity baselines. Provide turn-key engineering design submittals, professional installation, and cabling compliant with TIA and NEC standards during facility modifications, retrofits, and site expansions. title: Engineering Services for the B-52H Stratofortress
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL/QUOTE. This synopsis is not to be construed as a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract nor does the Government intend to directly pay for any information or responses submitted as a result of this solicitation. This is a Sources Sought Synopsis; there is no solicitation available at this time. This Sources Sought Synopsis is published for market research purposes only. Companies may be contacted if further information is needed. This announcement constitutes a Sources Sought Synopsis to seek a contractor for future work pertaining to the B-52H engineering services starting 01 January 2028. The Boeing B-52H Stratofortress is an American long-range subsonic jet-powered strategic bomber. The B-52 was designed and built by Boeing, which has continued to provide support and upgrades. It has been operated by the United States Air Force (USAF) since 1955 and was flown by NASA from 1959 to 2007. The bomber can carry up to 70,000 pounds (32,000 kg) of weapons and has a typical combat range of around 8,800 miles (14,200 km) without aerial refueling. The sustainment of the B-52H currently includes the delivery of engineering design, engineering support, and technical support services crucial for the ongoing maintenance and operational readiness of the B-52H aircraft, including its components and associated support and test equipment. The original estimated minimum/maximum amount for the B-52H sustainment contracts was $1.15B over ten (10) years (2019-2028) for engineering services Contract efforts are subject to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.232-18 availability of funds. The sustainment contracts currently contain multiple contract types at the contract line-item level (e.g. firm fixed price, cost plus incentive fee, cost plus fixed fee, etc.) This Sources Sought Synopsis only addresses the B-52H engineering services requirements starting 01 January 2029. The contractor will be required to provide engineering support services that provide technical information and logistics resources to enable maintenance and operational readiness of 76 B-52H aircraft. Engineering services will be required at the following USAF operational bases: Tinker AFB, Oklahoma; Edwards AFB, California; Minot AFB, North Dakota, and Barksdale AFB, Louisiana. Additionally, the contractor shall provide engineering support at the Boeing facility Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, to reflect field service representative (FSR) support. The contractor will be required to perform the following recurring engineering services: - Program Management and Integration - Principal Point of Contact - Platform Website - Meetings, briefings, conferences, reviews, and Technical Interchange Meeting (TIMs) - Structures Working Group - Government Property and Material Management - Unique Identifier (UID) Requirements - Configuration Management - Data management, automation and Contract data Requirements Delivery (CDRL) and CDRL Quality - Engineering Data/Documents Files - Quality Assurance Program - Engineering Support - Aircraft Structural Integrity Program (ASIP) - Specialized Engineering Support - System Integration Lab (SIL) - Ground and Flight Test Engineering Support - Drawing Cleanup and Procurement Ready Drawing - Programmed Depot Maintenance (PDM) Repair Development - Voluntary Protection Program - Field Services Representative (FSR) The contractor will be required to perform the following Non-recurring Engineering (NRE) services support: - Performance Work Statement (PWS) and Statement of Work (SOW) - Expedited Acquisitioin Process (EAP) and Engineering Projects (EP) - Interim Contractor Support (ICS) - Over & Above (O&A) - Travel - Material - Data Requirements - Meetings, briefings, conferences, reviews, and Technical Interchange Meeting (TIMs) - Associate Contractors and Proprietary Information Agreements (PIA) - Quality Assurance and Quality Management System - Safety - System Engineering - Diminishing Manufacturing Sources (DMS) - Earned Value management (EVM)s - Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) It is critical that respondents include the degree to which they will require access to B-52H rights and the degree to which they have or are able to obtain B-52H rights from Boeing. The capabilities package should be brief and concise yet clearly demonstrate an ability to meet the stated requirements. Recent, relevant experience should be provided for each area. If a company is capable of some, but not all of the consolidated requirements stated in this Sources Sought Synopsis, please provide a response that explains the requirements for which you are capable. Teaming and/or subcontracting arrangements should be clearly delineated and previous experience in teaming must be provided. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this action is 541330, size standard is $25.5 million. Firms responding to this announcement should indicate whether they are a large business, other than small business, small business, small disadvantaged business (SDB), woman-owned small business (WOSB), economically disadvantaged women-owned small business (EDWOSB), 8(a)-certified business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB), veteran-owned small business (VOSB), or Historically Underutilized Business Zone small business (HUBZone). All prospective contractors shall be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database to be awarded a DoD contract. Note that the NAICS code for this requirement, if applicable to the company's capabilities, should be included in the company's NAICS code listing in SAM (www.sam.gov). The acquisition strategy has not yet been determined. Market research results will assist the Air Force in determining whether this requirement will be a full and open, a small business (or other socioeconomic) set aside, or a sole source acquisition. Note that, if there is sufficient demonstrated interest and capability among small business contractors, a key factor in determining if an acquisition will be a Small Business Set-Aside is that two or more potential small business prime contractors must be capable of performing at least 50% of the effort, as defined in FAR clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting. If it is determined that a small business set-aside is appropriate and your company anticipates submitting a proposal as the prime contractor for a small business set-aside, please provide specific details and rationale as to how compliance with FAR clause 52.219-14 would be achieved, including specific details regarding teaming arrangements, etc. If subcontracts are to be used, provide anticipated percentage of effort to be subcontracted and whether small or large businesses will be used. Teaming and/or subcontracting arrangements should be clearly delineated and previous experience in teaming must be provided. It is anticipated that appropriate security classifications for personnel and facilities will be required up to the Secret level in satisfying these performance requirements. It is also anticipated that the contractor will require access to special access information, receive and generate classified material and fabricate, modify or store classified hardware. Appropriate security requirements will be required before contract award. Companies may be contacted for further information as required to assess their capabilities. The B-52 Contracting Branch is surveying the market to determine if any sources are qualified to fulfil any or all the above-mentioned requirements. Interested firms should submit sufficient information (limit to 20 pages � 12-point font, single-spaced, 1" margins) which will permit assessment of technical capabilities in writing or electronically to Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, AFLCMC/WBK, Attn. Mr. Kurt McKay, 3001 Staff Drive, Tinker AFB, OK 73145. If there are any questions with regard to the contract please contact Kurt McKay, Contract Negotiator, AFLCM

title: 380 kV, Bonaduz-Sils (GR), remplacement des pylônes avifaune
description:
Les travaux de génie civil comprennent la réalisation ou le renforcement des fondations pour huit emplacements de pylônes. Pour sept pylônes, les fondations existantes seront agrandies, assainies et renforcées au moyen de micropieux. En raison de sa proximité avec un cours d’eau de surface, le pylône 1261x005 sera déplacé d’environ 40 m en direction du pylône 1261x004 et sera doté, à son nouvel emplacement, d’une fondation entièrement nouvelle renforcée au moyen de micropieux. Le pylône 1261x005 sera en outre rehaussé de 4 m et le pylône 1261x019 de 9 m.

L’étendue des prestations comprend notamment les travaux de démolition et de sécurisation nécessaires, l’aménagement des accès au chantier et des voies d’accès temporaires, les travaux d’excavation et de stabilisation des talus, la réalisation de micropieux, les travaux de bétonnage et de fondation, les travaux de mise à la terre ainsi que la remise en état complète des surfaces utilisées. Les montants d’angle des nouveaux pylônes de la ligne seront scellés dans les fondations en béton.

Les travaux seront réalisés en partie dans des zones sensibles du point de vue paysager et écologique ainsi que sur des terrains difficiles d’accès et escarpés. Les prescriptions spécifiques à chaque site concernant la protection de la nature, du paysage, des eaux et des sols, ainsi que les surfaces autorisées pour les accès, les installations de chantier et les travaux, doivent impérativement être respectées lors de l’exécution.


Pour des raisons géographiques, l’appel d’offres relatif aux travaux de génie civil est subdivisé en deux lots, comprenant chacun quatre emplacements de pylônes.


L’étendue détaillée des prestations ainsi que les exigences et les quantités spécifiques au projet figurent dans les documents d’appel d’offres.

title: Planificateur général SIA 32-53 pour la sous-station de Regensdorf
description:
La sous-station de 220 kV de Regensdorf est située dans la commune de Regensdorf, dans le canton de Zurich.


L'installation de commutation de 220 kV à isolation gazeuse de la sous-station de Regensdorf a été mise en service en 2021. Malgré le jeune âge de l'installation à isolation gazeuse (5 ans), celle-ci ne peut pas, selon le fabricant, être étendue avec le même type d'installation. Une pièce d'adaptation fabriquée sur mesure est nécessaire pour pouvoir procéder à l'extension vers un type d'installation actuel. Cela s'accompagne d'un besoin d'espace plus important, raison pour laquelle Swissgrid a décidé d'agrandir directement l'installation de deux baies. À cette fin, l'installation GIS doit être agrandie de deux baies (baie de transformateur et baie de réserve), ainsi que des raccordements de câbles nécessaires.


Le présent appel d'offres vise à recruter le planificateur général pour les phases SIA 32 à 53 afin d'assurer la planification et la coordination de ce projet, les phases SIA 51 à 53 étant attribuées à titre optionnel. Outre l'étendue des prestations spécifiques à son domaine de compétence, le maître d'œuvre assume également la supervision et la coordination générales de tous les domaines spécialisés impliqués, y compris les interfaces associées, en tant que responsable général au sens de la norme SIA 103.


Les sous-projets suivants doivent être organisés par le planificateur général:


  • Direction et coordination de tous les domaines spécialisés impliqués, y compris les interfaces
  • Ingénierie et planification dans le sous-projet - Techniques des circuits primaires
  • Ingénierie et planification dans le sous-projet - Besoins propres
  • Ingénierie et planification dans le sous-projet - Bâtiment et génie civil
  • Direction des trauvaux (facultatif)


Les sous-projets suivants sont mis à la disposition du planificateur général:


  • Coordination générale des modèles BIM
  • Ingénierie et planifcation dans le sous-projet - Système d'automatisation des sous-stations (SAS)
  • Conception et planification dans le sous-projet - Environnement



Pour plus d'informations, veuillez consulter les documents C100 et C101 du dossier d'appel d'offres.

Det primære formål med projektet er at få valideret Danmarks Fængslers arealer og anvendelse af disse. Derudover er formålet med, scanningen, opmålingen og modelleringen at etablere et digitalt og datadrevet fundament for fremtidig ejendomsdrift, vedligehold, planlægning og udvikling. Projektet omfatter scanning, opmåling og opbygning af 3D-modeller (Revit/IFC), som skal kunne integreres i det nyligt indkøbte FM system (Dalux FM). Ejendomsporteføljen består af bygninger fordelt over hele Danmark. Porteføljen spænder bredt og inkluderer både nyere og ældre bygninger med stor arkitektonisk og teknisk variation. Den dækker en lang række anvendelsesformål – herunder, fængsler, arrester, boliger, tekniske anlæg og administration.

description: Das Schillerplatzareal in Iserlohn befindet sich im Zentrum der Stadt und stellt eine der wichtigsten Entwicklungsflächen im Rahmen der städtischen Erneuerungsstrategie dar. Ziel ist es, die städtebauliche Qualität und die Nutzungsvielfalt im Innenstadtbereich nachhaltig zu verbessern und die Funktion des Schillerplatzes als urbanes Zentrum zu stärken. Das Areal umfasst rd. 12.000 m² und liegt in direkter Nachbarschaft zu Rathaus, Stadt-Sparkasse, Stadthotel und Fußgängerzone, welche zugleich die südliche Grenze des Areals bildet. Dadurch ist eine direkte Anbindung an die wichtigsten innerstädtischen Verkehrs- und Aufenthaltsbereiche gewährleistet. Im Vorfeld der geplanten Entwicklung wurden bereits wesentliche vorbereitende Maßnahmen auf der Projektfläche durchgeführt, darunter der Abriss der ehemaligen Karstadt-Immobilie und der zugehörigen Tiefgarage sowie die Erkundung und Sicherung unterirdischer Hohlräume (Verkarstung und Erz-Bergbau). Unmittelbar an das Projektareal angrenzend (nördliche Seite des Theodor-Heuss-Rings) befindet sich derzeit das Rathaus I. Mit dem Abbruch des Rathaus I. wird voraussichtlich noch in 2026 begonnen. Zielvorgaben, Umfang und terminliche Umsetzung für einen möglichen Neubau an diesem Ort sind noch nicht bekannt. Das Schillerplatzareal und sein Umfeld bieten somit die Voraussetzungen für eine umfassende städtebauliche Entwicklung und das Projektareal stellt einen zentralen Baustein für die zukünftige Gestaltung und Nutzung der Iserlohner Innenstadt dar.
